title: Pool Telemetry Operator — Mini Slate & Burst Policy Wizard
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Design a compact operator "mini slate" for Redwood Console that surfaces GPU pool telemetry and an inline Burst Policy Wizard. The slate must fit as a right-rail contextual panel in the Dedicated Capacity view and enable on-call engineers and platform owners to quickly assess pool health, apply burst overrides, and tune autoscale hysteresis without navigating to a separate modal.

Goals:
- Present a dense but scannable telemetry summary (utilization, queue depth, tail latency, eviction rate, reserve headroom, recent scale events).
- Provide an inline Burst Policy Wizard that guides operators through safe burst configuration (duration, target headroom, cost cap, cooldown/hysteresis).
- Surface cost estimates for burst scenarios and show immediate delta to per-token or per-minute billing.
- Offer quick rollback and canary toggles; integrate with rollout controls so changes can be applied as canaries to a subset of pools.
- Maintain accessibility and keyboard-first interactions for incident workflows.

User stories:
- As an SRE, I want to see a one-glance health bar and last-5m spike overlays so I can triage a pool under load.
- As a platform engineer, I want to configure a temporary burst for a specified window and set an automated rollback so production cost and latency SLOs are preserved.
- As an on-call, I want to preview the cost impact and required headroom before applying a burst.

Key metrics to display (compact):
- GPU Utilization (avg over 1m, 5m)
- Request Queue Depth (current)
- P50/P95 Token Latency (ms)
- Eviction/Preemption Count (last 1h)
- Reserve Headroom (% of reserved capacity available)
- Autoscale Activity (scale up/down events timeline)

Prototype flows included in Figma links: three variants — "Conservative Mini" (text-first, small sparkline), "Interactive Tuner" (knobs for burst duration/cost cap), and "Incident Quickburst" (one-click presets for common incident responses). Prototype covers keyboard navigation, success/failure toast flows, and rollback actions.

Acceptance criteria:
- High-fidelity mini slate prototype implemented in Figma with all three variants and annotated interaction states.
- Usability test with 5 platform/SRE respondents showing task completion (apply burst, preview cost, rollback) >= 85% success.
- Engineering handoff deck with token definitions, color semantics, and interaction spec.
- Integration checklist prepared for ENG with required telemetry feeds (per-pool util, queue length, recent scale events) and sample API payloads for preview cost calculation.

Trade-offs and design decisions:
- Chose a compact horizontal health ribbon rather than a full vertical timeline to preserve vertical space in the Dedicated Capacity list view. This favors quick triage over deep historical analysis (deep dives still available in the full Pool Detail page).
- Burst Wizard exposes cost cap and duration but hides lower-level kernel/quantization toggles to reduce risk surface in the UI; those advanced knobs remain in an expert mode behind a feature flag.
- To avoid accidental cost spikes, any burst with estimated 24h cost delta > $500 requires a second confirmation and will default to canary rollout.

Implementation notes for ENG:
- Telemetry sampling: 1s granularity aggregated to 1m for sparkline, 5m window for summary tiles.
- Expose an API endpoint POST /pools/{id}/burst-requests with fields: duration_minutes, target_headroom_pct, cost_cap_usd, canary_pct. (PR spec linked in attachments).
- Include optimistic UI state and idempotency key for safe retries.

Links & artifacts:
- Figma prototype: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz/mini-slate-burst-wizard
- PRD (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/minislate-burst-wizard

- Telemetry dashboard template (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/POOL_TELEMETRY/minislate-template

2) Iterate on prototype based on SRE usability study (scheduled 2026-03-05).
3) Finalize handoff and produce React component spec for Console team (deadline 2026-03-18).

design_decision: Prefer compact, glanceable telemetry with inline action flows. Bursts default to canary and require explicit confirmation for high-cost deltas. Advanced tuning behind feature flag to reduce accidental operational risk.
notes: Prototype emphasizes keyboard accessibility and minimal modal usage to streamline incident triage. Reserve a follow-up ticket for expert-mode tuning controls after initial rollout.
